figures.caption: Fig. 1. Electrochemical performances of the NCM85/LZC and NCM85/LPSC cells under different cutoff voltages. (a, b) Galvanostatic charge–discharge voltage proﬁles of the cells at the 1st, 3rd, 4th, 20th, 50th, 100th and 200th cycles under 4.2 V cutoff voltage, and (c) corresponding cycling performances at 0.2 C. (d, e) Galvanostatic charge– discharge voltage proﬁles of the cells at the 1st, 3rd, 4th, 20th, 50th, 100th and 200th cycles under 4.5 V cutoff voltage, and (f) corresponding cycling performances at 0.2 C. The composite cathodes of the cells consisted of 70 wt% NCM85 and 30 wt% SSEs (LZC or LPSC).
figures.src: Qi 2025 - Deciphering high-voltage limitations of halide and sulfide ASSLBs (J Energy Chem 103 926).pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 2. Effects of the incorporation of conductive carbon on properties of the cells at 4.5 V. (a) First cycle voltage proﬁles of the NCM85/LZC cells with different contents of VGCF at 0.1 C, (b) corresponding dQ/dV curves, and (c) cycling stabilities at 0.2 C. (d) First cycle voltage proﬁles of the NCM85/LPSC cells with different contents of VGCF at 0.1 C, (e) corresponding dQ/dV curves, and (f) cycling stabilities at 0.2 C. (g) Electronic conductivities of NCM85/LZC cathodes with different contents of VGCF. (h) GITT curves and corresponding Li+ diffusion coefﬁcient versus the charge capacities of the NCM85/LZC cells. (i) Schematic diagram of the effects of the introduction of conductive carbon into the composite cathodes.
figures.src: Qi 2025 - Deciphering high-voltage limitations of halide and sulfide ASSLBs (J Energy Chem 103 926).pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 3. (a) Schematic illustration of the effects of incorporating carbon and stabilizing interface on charge transfer kinetics within cycled NCM85/SSE electrodes. SEM images of the (b, c) bare NCM85 and (d, e) 1.0 wt% LZPO@NCM85 particles. (f) HRTEM images of 1.0 wt% LZPO@NCM85 particle surface. (g) HAADF-STEM images of 1.0 wt% LZPO@NCM85 particle surface and corresponding EDS mappings of Ni, Co, Zr, P, and O elements. XPS spectra of (h) O 1s, (i) Zr 3d, and (j) P 2p for 1.0 wt% LZPO@NCM85 powders.
figures.src: Qi 2025 - Deciphering high-voltage limitations of halide and sulfide ASSLBs (J Energy Chem 103 926).pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 4. Superior electrochemical performances of the LZPO@NCM85 over the bare NCM85 at 4.5 V. (a, b) Galvanostatic charge–discharge voltage proﬁles of the NCM85/LZC cells at the 1st, 3rd, 4th, 20th, 50th, 100th and 200th cycles. (c) Cycling performances at 0.2 C. (d, e) Galvanostatic charge–discharge voltage proﬁles of the NCM85/LPSC cells at the 1st, 3rd, 4th, 20th, 50th, 100th and 200th cycles. (f) Long-term cycling performances of LZPO@NCM85 at 0.5 C. (g) Rate capabilities of LZPO@NCM85 from 0.1 to 1.0 C. (h) Cycling performances of the LZPO@NCM85 cells with high-loading cathodes of 26.0 mg cm 2 at 0.2 C and 60 ℃. (i) Radar plots of the various electrochemical performance indicators for different cells at 4.5 V. The composite cathodes of all cells were composed of 68 wt% CAMs, 30 wt% SSEs, and 2 wt% VGCF. 931
figures.src: Qi 2025 - Deciphering high-voltage limitations of halide and sulfide ASSLBs (J Energy Chem 103 926).pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 5. Analyzing the interfacial chemical evolution of cathodes during electrochemical cycling. (a) Zr 3d and Cl 2p XPS spectra of the pristine NCM85/LZC cathode, cycled NCM85/LZC cathodes at 4.2 or 4.5 V, and cycled LZPO@NCM85/LZC cathode at 4.5 V. (b) S 2p and P 2p XPS spectra of the pristine NCM85/LPSC cathode, cycled NCM85/LPSC cathodes at 4.2 or 4.5 V, and cycled LZPO@NCM85/LPSC cathode at 4.5 V. The cycling number was set at 200 cycles at 0.2 C. 932
figures.src: Qi 2025 - Deciphering high-voltage limitations of halide and sulfide ASSLBs (J Energy Chem 103 926).pdf

figures.caption: Fig. 6. Calculated mutual reaction energies between the potential cathode/electrolyte interface composition of (a) NCM85/LZC interface, (b) NCM85/LPSC interface, and (c) LZPO@NCM85/SSEs (LZC or LPSC) interface. To simplify the calculations, NCM85 was substituted by LiNiO2. Density of states (DOS) values of selected elements and total elements of (d) ZrO2, (e) Li2SO4, and (f) LZPO. (g) Schematic diagrams of reaction mechanism within three types of cathode/electrolyte interfaces and their effects on electrochemical properties of the cells.
